title: Nourishing Smoky Ethiopian Turkey Neck Stew
description: A hearty, creamy stew that blends the smoky depth of char‑grilled turkey necks with earthy lentils and aromatic Ethiopian spices, finished in a bamboo steamer for a tender texture.
instructions: Preheat a charcoal grill to medium‑high and char the turkey necks until smoky on all sides, about 5 minutes per side.
Rinse the lentils in a fine mesh sieve until the water runs clear.
In a bowl, combine lentils, smoked paprika, berbere, tomato paste, coconut milk, chicken broth, maple syrup, garlic‑infused oil, lemon juice, and asafoetida; stir to coat the lentils evenly.
Place the charred turkey necks into the lentil mixture, nestling them among the lentils.
Transfer the mixture to a heat‑proof bowl that fits inside a bamboo steamer.
Steam the bowl in the bamboo steamer over gently simmering water for 45 minutes until the turkey is tender and flavors meld.
Remove the bowl from the steamer, stir the stew, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the stew hot, garnished with chopped cilantro if desired, alongside low‑FODMAP flatbread or a drizzle of extra coconut milk.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
